articles.title: Cowboys Need A Massive Bounce Back In Green Bay
articles.summary: After a Thursday night loss to Tampa Bay, the Dallas Cowboys face a tough test at Lambeau Field. Can the team recover before their next primetime game?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are reeling. That Thursday night loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was a total disaster. Seeing the team fall 24-16 at home was hard to watch. Now, the squad has to find a way to recover before they head to Lambeau Field for Week 6.

The schedule isn't getting any easier. The Cowboys will travel to play the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, October 18. That game kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. It is the second of three straight primetime games for the team. I don't like the look of this stretch. You can't keep playing on national TV and losing like that.

The trip to Wisconsin is going to be brutal. The Cowboys are looking for a win to get back into the win column. It is hard to feel good about the team right now. Even the experts are skeptical. Per Sports Illustrated, it is tough to believe any oddsmakers would back the 'Boys after that last performance.

The pressure is mounting. The team needs to show progress. If they can't win in Green Bay, the season might start sliding. The defense has to step up. We saw what happened against Tampa Bay. We can't let it happen again in a cold stadium.

If you are a Bucs fan, you have a reason to smile. The Bucs are resting after their big win. Bucs fans should watch the Saints and Vikings game. A Saints loss would tie them at 1-4 in the division. That would be a huge win for Tampa Bay's standings.

There is also plenty to scout for the future. The Steelers and Colts both sit at 2-2. Since the Bucs face the Steelers next Sunday, this game is a great chance to see what's coming. The Cowboys face the Packers on Sunday, October 18, and the eyes of the league will be on them.

articles.title: Blades Brown makes new history by earning PGA Tour card at just 19 years old
articles.summary: At just 19, Blades Brown has made golf history by earning his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour. This achievement sets him up for an exciting future...
articles.body:
At just 19, Blades Brown has made golf history by earning his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour. This achievement sets him up for an exciting future in professional golf .

Golf Channel celebrated Brown's achievement on X, saying, "The future is bright for Blades Brown." The post recognized him as the youngest player to earn a PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour.

This accomplishment is a big step in Brown's fast-growing career. Earning a PGA Tour card is a major goal for golfers because it lets them compete with some of the world's best on the sport's top stage.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Brown reached this milestone at 19, earlier than anyone else through the Korn Ferry Tour. This shows his strong potential as one of golf's rising young talents.

The Korn Ferry Tour is a key path to the PGA Tour, giving up-and-coming golfers a chance to prove themselves and move up to the top level. Brown's success shows how quickly a young player can rise when their results match their talent.

Brown's achievement gives golf fans a new young player to watch as the next generation steps up. Now that he has a PGA Tour card, he can compete with top players and keep improving his game at the highest level.

Earning a Tour card is a big achievement, but it's just the start of the next challenge. Brown will now try to turn this breakthrough into lasting success as he begins the next part of his career.

At 19, Brown has already made history. His success has put him in the spotlight and created excitement about what he might do next.

As Golf Channel said, the future looks bright for this young golfer.

articles.title: As US suspends Green card programme for Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL; Shark Tank India judge Anupam Mittal remembers 'Full Emotional Atyachar' he faced when he went to return his Green Card years ago
articles.summary: As the US suspends a key green card step for several major Indian IT firms, entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal
articles.body: As the US suspends a key green card step for several major Indian IT firms, entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal has shared how he gave up his own green card, and why he sees America's immigration turmoil as an opportunity for India. Recently, the US government suspended several major technology and outsourcing firms, including Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant and Capgemini, from the Permanent Labor Certification Programme (PERM), a key route used by employers to sponsor foreign workers for employment-based green cards. The action also affects Microsoft and Adobe, with US authorities stating that they will neither accept new applications nor process pending labour certification requests involving the companies.The move has raised concerns among thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed in the US technology sector. While the suspension does not affect existing H-1B visas, it could delay or block one of the most important pathways to permanent residency in the United States.Anupam Mittal recalls his own Green Card dilemmaIn a post shared on professional networking platform LinkedIn, Mittal shared a personal story about giving up his own Green Card years ago. Mittal said that, like many ambitious young Indians, he had once dreamed of building a life in America. He said he achieved that goal through a strong education, a successful job and financial success, becoming a multimillionaire within a few years."Within four years, I was a multimillionaire living the American dream. Then came the Green Card. I was ecstatic. But somehow the feeling was fleeting," he wrote. Mittal said that despite receiving permanent residency, he decided to move back to India in 2004 to build companies. However, he continued travelling to the US every year to maintain his residency status, even as he struggled with whether he should hold on to the Green Card.'The officer looked at me like I was crazy'The entrepreneur recounted visiting the US consulate in Mumbai to surrender the document. According to Mittal, the consular officer was surprised by his decision and urged him to reconsider."The officer looked at me like I was crazy. 'Think about this. Once you give it up, you may never get it back'," Mittal wrote. He jokingly described the exchange as "full emotional atyachar", adding that he ultimately walked out of the office with the Green Card still in his pocket.A year later, however, he returned and completed the process. "This time, I handed it over. And I walked out feeling lighter than I had in years. For the first time, both my feet were on the same side," he said.Mittal used the story to reflect on changing attitudes among Indian entrepreneurs and professionals. He said that had he remained in the United States, he might have become a wealthy technology executive. Instead, returning to India allowed him to build companies, invest in more than 300 startups and become part of the country's growing startup ecosystem.Read Anupam Mittal’s complete post hereLike most ambitious Indian kids, I dreamt of life in America.And I got there! Great education & job. More money than I had imagined.Within four years, I was a multimillionaire living the American dream. Then came the Green Card. I was ecstatic.But somehow the feeling was fleeting.So in 2004, I came back to India to build.But every year, I still flew back to the US to give 'hazri' & I struggled with the feeling.So I went to the consulate in Mumbai to surrender the Green Card.The officer looked at me like I was crazy.“Think about this. Once you give it up, you may never get it back.”Full emotional atyachar - walked out with it still in my pocket 😅A year later, I went back.This time, I handed it over.And I walked out feeling lighter than I had in years.For the first time, both my feet were on the same side. 🇮🇳Sometimes I wonder what would have happened if I had stayed.I probably would have been a wealthy VP at a tech company, eating once a week at an Indian restaurant worrying that AI would take my job.I would not have built the companies I did, backed 300+ Indian startups, or sat on @sharktank India watching new Indian founders dream bigger than we ever did.Which is why I look at the H-1B and Green Card turmoil in America differently.For decades, success meant a life in the USA. That story is finally breaking.And I think that's a very good thing🔥The time is here to build global tech & brand companies from India.Sometimes a closing door is what makes you realize where home is.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Golf: DP World Tour to refuse LIV players in 2027 season
articles.summary: The DP World Tour will not allow LIV Golf players to compete at its events in the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Players who sign up to LIV Golf next season will not be allowed to be members of the European tour in 2027.

The European tour, which is sponsored by DP World, said players must "make a choice" regarding where they play - a significantly tougher stance than in recent seasons.

Only players who are members of the DP World Tour can play for Europe in the Ryder Cup.

Deadlines for both tours are in the next five weeks, though there remains uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf's future despite it securing a possible $300m in funding as it attempts to restructure.

"Players need to make a choice," Guy Kinnings, CEO of the DP World Tour, told BBC Sport.

"We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

In previous years, conditional releases were struck with some top players - including Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton - enabling them to play on both the DP World Tour and LIV.

However, players will be asked to disclose which tours they intend to play on for next year, and their answer will be taken into account when deciding on their membership.

Rahm to leave LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms

Strained smiles and uncertainty - the strange end of LIV Golf 1.0

About 15 LIV players - including Rahm, Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin - have "status" with the DP World Tour, meaning they have eligibility under one of the membership categories.

Other LIV players, like Joaquin Niemann and Thomas Pieters, do not have such status so would either need to go through qualifying school or sign agreements with the DP World Tour by which they would receive invitations to a set number of tournaments.

However, those agreements would only be available to players who were not part of LIV in the future.

BBC Sport has been told the DP World Tour will not accept membership from anyone intending to play on what is being called LIV 2.0.

If players did not disclose their intention to play LIV and went on to do so, that would be considered grounds on which to have their membership terminated.

LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September as it attempted to restructure, following the withdrawal of its multi-billion dollar funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

Last week, it announced it had secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.

LIV equity offer changes DP World Tour's approach

While the DP World Tour agreed to grant conditional releases with nine players this season, it is understood the change for 2027 is predominantly down to LIV offering players equity in future and a feeling this is incompatible with the European tour being a members organisation.

However, it also comes at a time when the DP World Tour's strategic alliance with the PGA Tour is being negotiated, so the move likely reflects a desire to put itself in the best position possible in those discussions.

Players will have until 16 November to sign up to the DP World Tour for next year.

Under the terms of its court-supervised restructuring process, LIV Golf needs to sign players up by 25 October.

Ted Goldthorpe, head of BC Partners Credit, told BBC Sport last week he was "confident" LIV would have a "critical mass" of players.

But since then two-time major winner Rahm has said he will not continue playing on the LIV tour.

Lawyers representing a number of other players, including fellow major winners Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith, sought clarification from the court that rejection of contracts would equate to "termination", enabling players to hold discussions with third parties about their futures.

Richard Bland is currently the only player to have stated publicly a desire to play on LIV 2.0.

However, Perez indicated last month he hoped there would be a future for the league.

articles.title: DP World Tour to deny LIV Golf players memberships for 2027 season - players must now 'make a choice'
articles.summary: The DP World Tour has said it will deny LIV Golf players memberships if they take part in the league for 2027; players need to be on the DP World Tour to be eligible for the Ryder Cup; players must now "make a choice"
articles.body:
Some of the world's top players were given conditional releases by the European tour in previous seasons, allowing them to compete on both circuits.

But DP World Tour chief executive officer Guy Kinnings has said players must now "make a choice".

In order to be eligible for Europe's Ryder Cup team, players must be members of the DP World Tour.

Kinnings told BBC Sport : "Players need to make a choice. We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

LIV Golf chief executive Scott O'Neil has previously insisted that "one group of golfers" should not be "restricted from playing elsewhere".

LIV's future is in doubt after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew support at the end of the season and is going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States.

The breakaway series has secured an initial funding commitment for a potential $300m (£227m) investment from BC Partners Credit to help relaunch LIV 2.0 in 2027.

Deadlines for both tours fall next month and players will be asked to disclose which they intend to play on.

LIV players such as Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin are currently eligible to play on the DP World Tour under one of its membership categories.

Rahm is set to quit LIV Golf after refusing to accept new terms offered for its proposed relaunch and is reported to be owed up to $150m (£113m) for the remainder of the contract he signed almost three years ago.

articles.title: The Iran war didn't make your heating bill this high. Blue-state energy policy did
articles.summary: Blocked pipelines and refinery shortages explain why energy prices spike every winter, leaving families vulnerable to global oil market swings.
articles.body: Heating season is here, and the Iran war is getting the blame for higher energy prices. The war explains the timing. It doesn't explain the vulnerability. America produces enormous amounts of oil and gas. Why do prices jump when the Persian Gulf flares? Because oil trades on a world market. A crisis anywhere moves prices everywhere. But the real problem is policies at the state level that have kept us from truly unleashing the bounty of our domestic energy supply. CHEVRON CEO WARNS IRAN CONFLICT HAS CREATED 'VERY REAL' THREAT TO GLOBAL OIL SUPPLIES AS GAS PRICES CLIMB It’s been well documented that we have a refinery shortage. The country has 130 operable refineries, down from 301 in 1982, and no major new refinery has been built in the U.S. since 1976. Here in the Northeast, when we lost the Philadelphia Energy Solutions plant, we lost about 335,000 barrels a day. In my home state of New York, like so many other states, we also have a self-imposed supply problem. Natural gas moves through pipelines, and New York has blocked those pipelines. Pennsylvania, right next door, sits on some of the richest gas fields in the country. The Constitution Pipeline, if constructed, would carry that natural gas 124 miles, with 99 miles of new right-of-way in New York. AMERICAN BUSINESSES AREN’T ALLOWED TO BUILD. IT’S TIME CONGRESS HELPED THEM The fight to build this much-needed pipeline is now 10 years old. In April 2016, the state denied the water permit. Courts upheld it. The company tried again in 2025, then withdrew in November after three notices that its application was incomplete. And the problem runs deeper than one pipeline. Ill-conceived climate laws set sweeping emissions targets, and the plan to reach them is thin if not unattainable. Take New York City's Local Law 97. It fines large buildings that exceed emissions limits, and the limits tighten sharply in 2030. Owners must pay for costly retrofits or pay penalties. Either way, the bill lands on tenants, co-op owners and small businesses. THE REAL REASON YOUR ELECTRIC BILL IS SOARING THIS SUMMER WILL SURPRISE YOU Democrats in too many state capitals seem determined to choke off other reliable and cost-effective energy sources. Nuclear reactors and coal plants have closed down, both of which supply much-needed energy to citizens, especially low-income families. Meanwhile, the utility bills keep climbing, filling your gas tank becomes more painful, and truckers and shippers face punishing prices for diesel, which, of course, trickles down to raise the cost of everything from lumber to lunch meat. SENATORS PRESS PRESIDENT TRUMP TO RELEASE HOME HEATING OIL RESERVES AMID SOARING PRICES I’ve spent over 20 years in the energy and utility industry. Energy is not abstract. It is pipe, wire, steel and supply. Limit supply while demand holds, and prices rise. That is arithmetic, not ideology. And winter makes it more brutal. On the coldest days, when pipes run full, utilities scramble for alternatives and alternatives cost more. Families on fixed incomes can't opt out. They lower the thermostat and pull on another sweater. TRUMP ADMIN MOVES TO GUT BIDEN'S SIGNATURE ENVIRONMENTAL RULES Here is what should bother everyone, whatever their politics. A state that won't produce or import its own fuel doesn't become independent. It becomes a customer. It bids against the world for supply and accepts whatever price is asked, including prices set by wars it can't influence. The fight to build this much-needed pipeline is now 10 years old. In April 2016, the state denied the water permit. Courts upheld it. The company tried again in 2025, then withdrew in November after three notices that its application was incomplete. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION What's the solution? Approve pipeline projects with capacity that bring in domestic gas. Keep reliable power plants running until real replacements are built and tested. Approve the construction of new refineries. Be honest about what climate mandates cost and phase them in at a pace working families can afford. Judge success by lower bills and steady supply, not ribbon-cuttings. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And most importantly: Vote for candidates this November who are dedicated to American energy independence, supporting sensible and robust expansion of both production and refinement of our own bountiful energy supply.

articles.title: Ultimátum a los jugadores de LIV Golf
articles.standfirst: El DP World Tour no permitirá que se compaginen sus torneos con los de LIV Golf 2.0
articles.summary: El DP World Tour no permitirá que se compaginen sus torneos con los de LIV Golf 2.0
articles.body: LIV Golf 2.0 todavía no ha nacido y no sabemos ni tan siquiera si verá la luz pese a los 300 millones de dólares que está dispuesta a invertir la financiera BC Partners. El motivo no es otro que la cantidad de dificultades que va a tener para que haya jugadores que continúen ligados al proyecto. La nueva versión de la superliga tiene previsto un calendario de 10 torneos, cinco de ellos en Estados Unidos. Hasta aquí todo bien, pero existe un gran problema: la temporada de cualquier jugador se compone de al menos 25 torneos, por lo que para llegar a este número sería necesario competir en otro/s circuito/s. Por supuesto, el PGA Tour (circuito estadounidense) no está dispuesto a abrir la mano y el DP World Tour tampoco lo va a hacer, según ha declarado su director ejecutivo a la BBC. El caso es que este año el DPWT acordó con algunos de sus miembros que también jugaban en la superliga, que no los sancionaría a cambio de acudir a determinados torneos. Pues bien, dicha ‘bula’ ya no se va a prorrogar en 2027. "Los jugadores tienen que tomar una decisión", declaró Guy Kinnings, CEO del DP World Tour, a BBC Sport. "Tenemos normas y reglamentos que existen para proteger nuestro circuito y que todos nuestros miembros deben cumplir. Los jugadores que no estén dispuestos a cumplir con nuestras reglas y regulaciones no deberían intentar unirse a nuestro circuito". Queda claro que el DPWT ya no aceptará a jugadores del LIV; se terminó ese intento de coexistir que sólo ha durado un año. Es la puntilla para LIV Golf 2.0, pues habrá muchos jugadores que descarten unirse a un circuito de solo 10 eventos y cuya membresía conlleva demasiados perjuicios. Ya sabemos que Jon Rahm ha descartado unirse a LIV 2.0 y que su futuro está en el DP World Tour a menos que alcance algún acuerdo con el PGA Tour. Sergio García ya se desligó de LIV y tiene muy claro que su lugar es regresar el Circuito Europeo para intentar jugar la Ryder Cup. David Puig tiene estatus para jugar el año que viene en el DPWT y ya ha dicho que tampoco seguirá en LIV. Hay jugadores que pertenecen al Circuito Europeo como Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez o Tom McKibbin que aún se deben pronunciar pero, por ejemplo, Joaquín Niemann está ahora en tierra de nadie. En el caso de Josele Ballester, puede competir en el Asian Tour porque ya ganó allí, pero está intentado acceder al DPWT a través de la escuela. Una de las grandes incógnitas es que será de Phil Mickelson, que este año sólo jugó el LIV Golf Sudáfrica en marzo, y por tanto en esas fechas el año que viene podría estar ya en el Champions Tour (circuito de veteranos del PGA Tour).

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's daughter ditches Ole Miss & LSU to root for new SEC team, Dolphins fans attack & sad Eagles kid
articles.summary: Screencaps, America's Best Daily Column, tackles Landry Kiffin wearing UT colors at the Red River Shootout while her dad's LSU season spiraled.
articles.body: Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun. Landry Kiffin is the poster child for the SEC fans who were known to chant "SEC, SEC, SEC" before NIL evened the playing field PICK A TEAM! While her dad's season was spiraling out of control Saturday night in Lexington, Kentucky, Landry was in Texas rooting for the No. 1 team in the nation in the Red River Shootout. "U win some u lose some," Landry wrote on TikTok when questioned about her ability to pick a winning team in the SEC. In another video, Landry added, "And go Tigers. We'll be watching at a bar when that game starts." UNRANKED OKLAHOMA KNOCKS OFF NO. 1 TEXAS IN WALK-OFF FASHION AFTER ARCH MANNING'S ROUGH 4TH QUARTER Why go to a UT game and wear UT colors when your dad has to play this team on Nov. 14? "Spying," she wrote. Imagine Nick Saban's daughter openly rooting for a rival SEC program back in like 2010 while her father was in the middle of absolute wars to win the league. This is where we're at with this TikTok generation. Just like the players and coaches in the NIL era, the influencer daughters aren't loyal either. LANE KIFFIN'S DAUGHTER DISGUSTED BY 'VULGAR' BED SHEET BANNERS ACCUSING HER OF HAVING SEX WITH A PLAYER 📩 Email: joe.kinsey@outkick.comSend photos, stories, tips, rants—whatever you've got. 📰 Screencaps Page:👉 Read the latest Screencaps ▶️ YouTube: Screencaps with Joe KinseySubscribe for videos, rants, and behind-the-scenes. 🐦 Twitter/X: @JoeKinseyexpTag me or drop a DM. 📸 Instagram: @OutKickScreencapsYou guys need to start tagging me on content you're seeing. 📘 Facebook Page: Screencaps on Facebook 👥 Facebook Group: Join the Screencaps Community 📬 Mail (Thursday Night Mowing League):27072 Carronade Dr, Unit A 155Perrysburg, OH 43551 🗞️ Newsletter:👉 Subscribe here Speaking of LSU, make this AP poll make sense...Landry clearly knows her season is over, so now she's trying to find a new bandwagon to hop on for the playoffs LSU has beaten a terrible Clemson program and a terrible Texas A&M team. Even the biggest of you SEC homers know that LSU shouldn't be getting this sort of respect. Random emails on a Monday morning – Lee D. in Tampa writes: Good genes. Kinsey: Based on my research, I don't believe there's ever been a mother-daughter sideline reporting tandem to work an NFL game. If we go even further, the NFL, to my knowledge, has never had a mother-daughter-daughter sideline reporting TRIO. Melissa's daughters are twins. One goes to Auburn and the other goes to Stanford. NFL QB & CHEERLEADER SISTER BELIEVED TO BE LEAGUE'S FIRST SIBLING DUO, BOAT RAMP FIGHT & EDDIE GEORGE'S HOUSE Will they go into the family business? Stay tuned. – Greg in Nebraska checks in: I read Screencaps Thursday and saw what you had written about signs in yards changing opinions. When I read it I was definitely a no. That would never impact my vote. Friday morning I was taking my daughter to school and saw a sign for a candidate that I know and was going to vote for in the yard a of a lefty house and now I’m a yes it will change my mind. The guy I thought I was voting for is the dad of a guy I worked with a few years ago. Met the dad a couple of times and he was a good guy so I was ok with voting for him. After I looked up what he supports, I’m voting for the other guy. I’m glad the lefty house had his sign or i would never have looked him up and would have voted for the wrong guy. – Gen X. Warren in Florida has a message for the Dolphins: Congrats to the Bengals on their W. I hope someone in the Ross family, owners of the Miami Dolphins, sees this. SELL THE TEAM! No one trusts you to make good decisions. No coach wants to work for you, no matter the money, because it’s such a toxic environment. But you’re making too much money to care (stadium). Sell the team to an owner who cares, and save the legacy! Us fans need to demand more, per Armando last year. I’d say we’ll protest, but Mrs. Gen X Warren M. is a Lions fan, so we’re going to Lions at Miami game next month… – Susan G. says: I truly believe the Dallas Cowboys will not be a winning team again until Jerry passes away and they replace Dak. I know I know he has a great pass completion percentage but he can’t do it when it counts. I am 67 years old and I have been a Cowboys fan since I can remember, but these days I don’t expect them to win. It is really sad! Golf integrity is one of the biggest issues of our lives right now How do I know? Wait until you see how many emails this topic generated over the weekend. Normally, I'll get maybe six emails on a hot topic over a weekend because you guys have lives to live. This weekend, it was completely different. We have ourselves a hot topic. – Kevin W. emails: I love the question about golf integrity. I belong to a private club, and it's a constant debate. We like other clubs have a "men's day" where all the tee times that day put money into a pot and play various games. This is where the convenience of technology created an issue. We, like yourself, and lots of other golf clubs, started using Golf Genius. Nice and convenient to enter scores; HOWEVER, it also posts scores as they are happening. So, what happens when the guys who go off early post a good score? The late guys see the number they have to beat and BINGO, suddenly 5-footers are good, and those groups are winning everything. Our club's first solution to the problem was to buy a very expensive software called CAP patrol from a bunch of data scientists. Basically, it was the socialist version of golf handicaps that punished good golfers to even out the field for the higher handicappers. It would cherry-pick low rounds and say you're better than your index and you MUST BE cheating otherwise. There were a ton of other factors, and nobody understood the algorithm of who got capped and who didn't, and the company wouldn't disclose it. It's very popular with private clubs on the east and west coasts. We quickly scrapped it. The simple solution this year was to go old school and stop the live scoreboard. Pretty much fixed the issue. In general, if you want to fix giving short putts, always have a money game going. My group of guys rarely, if ever, just go out and play a round just to play. We always have some dollars on the line; even if it's just a few bucks, it keeps the integrity there, as a short putt can change a game quickly. Just my $.02 – Rural MN Dave agrees: I played in a group for many years that played strict rules of golf and no gimmes. One of the group members was playing on a 9 handicap but was really closer to a 6. The strength of his game was chipping and putting. One day he had an 18 inch birdie putt with several skins carryovers riding on it. He stepped up to the putt, taking his time and doing his regular routine, and cold yanked it, never even touched the hole. He looked up, red-faced, and said "and that's why we don't do gimmes!" – Michael in Bossier City, Louisiana says: Your recent article on shaving golf scores did not shock me the least bit. I believe that gimmie putts really skew one’s score when playing the same course conditions. However, not all course conditions are equal. Do you play on a goat ranch city course or a private near PGA standards. I would love to witness a professional golfer score scratch or better on the city course I play regularly; bare fairways and tree roots jutting out in all directions. Rolling the ball slightly to find that last remaining few blades of grass in the fairways or safety setting away from tree roots that are three inches exposed to the surface becomes a must for sanity; you are still accountable to that next golf shot. Now, I’ve played in regional and state tournaments that would white mark a tenth of my course as no play areas because of root or extreme bare spot areas. Then again, I’m not disagreeing with you on most of your points of play. If you are behind a tree or in the rough, then you need to hit your best way out and onto the green to putt it out. More to note! I’m a 6.8 handicap in which I play a fairly nice city course other than the tree root issues and played Robert Trent courses resulting in a near score equivalence. Yes, plugging in the rough off the fairway, moving your ball for a way out of tree trouble and taking gimmie putts does mask one’s real ability. However, having a fake lower handicap which most tournaments only take 85% to prevent sandbaggers will hurt a delusional golfer in the end. Well, hope you had time to read my opinion. – Joyce tells us about her club's gimme rule: Just think how many games and championships Ohio State would have won if the 3-foot gimme rule would have been in play for field goals and touchdowns. Last year our women's golf league finally adopted a 6-inch gimme rule, a measurement that we can easily imagine. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Is the weather in the Smoky Mountains where all the COVID transplants moved actually overrated? Look at the map and then look at NW Ohio where I live compared to the heart of the Smoky Mountains. I never would've thought I'm in a better comfortable weather location compared to the Smokies, but the data says otherwise. – Chris B. in NC, formerly Florida, tells me: Here in the Smokies at 5,000’, we won’t get up to 60 very often from later this month until some time in March or even April. Also, it rains a lot, which is why everything here is so green and lush compared to the Rockies. It’s pretty rare to have a clear warm day during these months. As for south Florida: the highs will be over 87 by early May and won’t really drop until nearly Thanksgiving. East coast is a little warmer than west, but you’ve been on the Gulf side in the summer. It’s steamy. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. The reason its called the Smoky’s is there are plenty of days where you have fog/mist covering the mountains, especially near lakes, giving it a look of smoke. Most of the time it burns off by mid morning in the summers but other times it can hang around. So guessing this effects the poster’s criteria of cloud cover. Given the temp range and low dew point, the poster skewed the results to make a small strip of the west coast look ideal. Maybe the guy lives there and wants bragging rights. As someone that lived a part of his childhood in California and most of his life in Louisiana, moving to East Tennessee over 8 years ago has been fantastic weather wise (and just about any other wise). I live in that sweet spot where you experience all 4 seasons with each lasting about 3 months. Unlike LA where you had 50 weeks of summer, 1 of spring and fall, and 1 day of winter. articles.title: DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players, ending Ryder Cup eligibility
articles.summary: The DP World Tour is banning LIV Golf members from competing in its events starting in 2027, another blow to LIV Golf's future.
articles.body:
The DP World Tour is banning LIV Golf members from competing in its events starting in 2027.

Unlike the PGA Tour—which had suspended LIV players since LIV launched in 2022—the DP World Tour had been granting LIV players conditional releases to participate in tournaments. It was a move that was partially done in order to keep several LIV individuals eligible for the Ryder Cup, as the DP World Tour overseas the European team. That included a settlement earlier this year with Tyrrell Hatton and (after a prolonged public fight) Jon Rahm paying outstanding fines for defecting to the former Saudi league. RELATED: Jon Rahm's LIV Golf gamble is over and nobody won

However, those still with LIV must apply for DP World Tour membership by Nov. 16, and guidelines now stipulate that double-dipping between tours is not allowed. More than a dozen LIV players had status on both tours, including Rahm, Hatton and Tom McKibbin.

In a statement to the BBC, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said, "Players need to make a choice. We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

In August, LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil asserted LIV wanted to "complete, not compete" the golf ecosystem, a comment that upset DP World Tour officials after LIV tried to poach several DP World Tour tournaments and sponsors. Additionally, O'Neil accused a DP World Tour leader of contacting LIV players to discuss their options; subsequent reporting indicated it was actually player agents contacting the DP World Tour.

Last week Rahm's attorneys told a New Jersey bankruptcy court that Rahm does not want to be part of LIV's future. Hatton, who has made four Ryder Cup appearances for Team Europe, has not made his intentions public.

Aside from Rahm, Sergio Garcia was granted an exit from his contract and fellow Spaniard David Puig said he was no longer interested in playing with LIV. Attorneys for Cam Smith, Matt Wolff and others asked the court whether Garcia's request sets a precedent for their clients.

Also last week, LIV's new investor, BC Partners, extended the deadline for players to sign up for the league to Oct. 25. "We're super committed," BC Partners CEO Ted Goldthorpe said at a London conference. "As [LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil] said, we're going to start hiring back employees and planning for next year's events. All systems go.

"The next 22 days will be about signing up the players, and I feel very good about that. We've had a lot of constructive dialogue with them. We obviously have a deadline now, but that's the next big step for us."

However, there are questions if BC Partners is truly interested in running the league, as it has a history of taking on trouble companies for future tax credits. The next bankruptcy hearing is scheduled for this Wednesday.

articles.title: Michael Brennan is officially a dude, Blades Brown is coming and time is Jon Rahm's best friend
articles.summary: Michael Brennan's third PGA Tour win at the Baycurrent Classic vaults him to world No. 20 in what's been a quiet yet meteoric rise for the star.
articles.body: The PGA Tour has always had the great problem of having so much young talent that many up-and-comers fall through the cracks and don't get the attention they deserve until they quietly put together a resume that suddenly smacks you in the face. Nobody on Tour right now may optimize that more than Michael Brennan. On the topic of young talent, Blades Brown is headed to the PGA Tour next year. At just 19 years old and some change, he's the youngest player ever to earn his Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour after finishing ninth on the season-long points list. In other news, LIV Golf suffered a haymaker amid its bankruptcy mess, with Jon Rahm officially opting to split with the league as its future remains entirely up in the air. While it's so easy to look at the (many) negatives involving Rahm and his run with LIV, there is a very obvious yet important reality to look forward to. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. Michael Brennan deserves your respect When you think of young stars on Tour, let's call it guys who are 26 or younger, the likes of Jackson Koivun (21), Akshay Bhatia (24), Tom Kim (24), Michael Thorbjornsen (25), Jacob Bridgeman (26), and Ludvig Aberg (26) immediately come to mind, and rightfully so. After what 24-year-old Michael Brennan accomplished in Japan over the weekend, his name firmly belongs in that group. The Baycurrent Classic marked Brennan's 33rd career start on the PGA Tour, and after beginning Sunday's final round tied for the lead, he went out and posted a 3-under 68 to earn a one-shot victory, giving him three career wins, all coming in under 12 months' time. Brennan's maiden win came at the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship in November against an admittedly weaker field. His second trip to the winner's circle, a three-shot victory, came this August at the Wyndham Championship against a stronger crop of players fighting for a spot into the FedEx Cup Playoffs. While the Wyndham could be described as his first "big boy" win, his victory at the Baycurrent, on international soil, is the most impressive of the three, as he held off the likes of Xander Schauffele, Brian Harman, Ryan Gerard, Keith Mitchell, and Bridgeman en route to victory. Brennan was ranked 61st in the world in late July, but has catapulted himself all the way to No. 20 in what can only be described as a quiet, yet meteoric rise. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The former Wake Forest star turned professional in 2024, made quick work of the PGA Tour Americas circuit in 2025 with three wins to earn a spot on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2026, but ultimately skipped that step. His start in the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship came via a sponsor's exemption, and he went out and won the event, his first career start on Tour as a pro, by four shots. So, about a year into his professional career, Brennan had already earned a PGA Tour membership, and less than a year on from that maiden victory, he's earned two more wins. He also made the cut in all four major championships in 2026, which is something only 13 other players can say they accomplished. The Virginia native has proven he knows how to do the hardest part – actually win – and also happens to rank second and third, respectively, in average club head speed and driving distance on Tour. Brennan is one of the best young players on the planet, period. Blades Brown keeps meeting huge expectations It's safe to say Blades Brown made the right call skipping out on that whole college experience thing. Since before he could drive a car, which admittedly wasn't all that long ago, the expectation for Blades Brown has simply been 'the next guy.' While he hasn't won a professional event at this point in his insanely young career, he's just about met every expectation out there. It has been a steady climb for the Nashville native since he made his professional debut in January 2025 at 17 years old at The American Express. He's made the most out of countless sponsors' exemptions on the PGA Tour and put together an incredibly consistent campaign on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2026 with six Top 10s and just two missed cuts in 18 starts, which was plenty to earn a spot on Tour in 2027. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE When the calendar flips in January, things get as real as possible for a guy who doesn't turn 20 until May, but Brown has shown absolutely no reason to doubt him as he's been Mr. Consistent. In 11 starts on Tour in 2026, Brown missed just two cuts, finished solo third at the Puerto Rico Open, and picked up a total of seven Top 25 finishes. His career is very simply on the exact, consistent trajectory many expected it to be on at this point. Currently ranked 97th in the world, it will be fascinating to see how Brown plays out of the gates in 2027. Sneaking inside the Top 50 and earning a Masters invite would be quite the story. We'll eventually not care about Jon Rahm's stint on LIV It's so easy to say that Jon Rahm made a mistake when he left the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2024. You could claim it was a decision made out of greed, as he made the move for hundreds of millions of dollars. Then again, 99.9% of humanity would leave one job for another to acquire generational wealth, plus, Rahm was up front that money was the major factor behind his decision to join the then Saudi-backed circuit. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER You could also claim that the move hurt his reputation. He made the jump at just 30 years old in the prime of his career with two major championships already in his back pocket. While it's fair to focus on those aspects now, our now will soon become our then, and Rahm has an ample amount of time to make his brief career on LIV Golf seem like a forgettable blip on his resume. While at this point in time we don't know how he'll do it, the Spaniard will get back to competing on the PGA Tour against the best players in the world on a consistent basis. Maybe we see that in six months, maybe it takes 18 months, who knows, but when it happens, it'll be a jolt to the PGA Tour from every angle. Yes, two decades from now, golf fans will make jokes about Rahm leaving for LIV Golf for a couple of years while remembering him making the announcement in a ridiculous letterman jacket, but our level of caring about it at that point, in the grand scheme of things, won't even exist.

articles.title: 'Validation and relief' for Forrest after Spanish Open win
articles.summary: Grant Forrest on dealing with last hole nerves in Madrid and the euphoria of the biggest win of his career.
articles.body:
"I don't think I've ever been as nervous on a golf course."

Scotland's Grant Forrest knocked in a last-hole birdie at the Spanish Open on Sunday to seal the biggest win of his career.

Along with the £480,000 first prize come places at the Masters and The Open next year.

It has also propelled the 33-year-old up 156 places the world rankings to 140th.

Playing partner Victor Perez missed his chance to overtake clubhouse leader Eugenio Chacarra, leaving the door open for Forrest to claim his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

"When the stage was set for me to try and hole the winning putt, my hands were shaking," he told BBC Scotland.

"I don't know how I managed to make it go in. Delighted that it did, obviously.

"You just fall back into your routine. Breathing has been a huge part of what I've worked on recently - and that really helped throughout the whole day."

Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win

DP World Tour to refuse LIV players in 2027 season

Forrest has not had much sleep over "a surreal 24 hours" as he flew from Madrid to New Dehli for the DP World India Championship.

Having made his professional bow over a decade ago, he said the victory brought "a lot of validation, relief as well."

On the prospect of a Masters debut in April, he explained: "I was there as a spectator in 2019 and it's just an incredibly special place.

"To have the opportunity to play hasn't sunk in yet."

Forrest has had experience of The Open in 2013 and 2018, at Muirfield and Carnoustie respectively.

"Playing a third at St Andrews is going to be incredible," he added.

Forrest graduated from the European Challenge Tour to the DP World Tour at the end of the 2018 season along with compatriots Robert MacIntyre and David Law.

Connor Syme and Scott Jamieson have won titles in the past two years, along with Ryder Cup star MacIntyre.

"It gives you positive energy when one guy succeeds," Forrest said on the current strength of Scottish golf.

"You know they are not much different in terms of ability, it's just reminding yourself that a win can be round the corner at any point."

This week's polls are for outstanding athletic accomplishments from Oct. 5-10.

Voting can be completed through the two ballots listed below. Voting closes at midnight Thursday, Oct. 15.

articles.title: Bears get optimistic news on Caleb Williams amid potential Week 6 return
articles.summary: This Caleb Williams update is a very encouraging sign for Week 6.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears lost Caleb Williams near the end of Week 2 in their loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and the combination of Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent has gone 2-1 since then.

But after a rough Week 5 against the NFC North rival Green Bay Packers , the Bears are in desperate need of Williams back on the field. Fortunately, the latest update is some good news for such a future coming to pass.

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network , the Bears' QB is trending in the right direction, and that "all signs" are pointing towards Williams returning to the Bears' offense this upcoming Week 6 matchup.

Bears get good Caleb Williams news for Week 6 playing odds

"The fact that Caleb Williams was working out before the game, in a pretty strenuous workout... this is a very good sign," Rapoport said. "... All signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field for Chicago..."

With a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on tap, the Bears getting Williams back would be huge. After missing three weeks, he's one week away from missing the equivalent amount of time as if he were placed on injured reserve.

Returning for Week 6 against the Falcons would prove the Bears were right not to place Williams on IR. They shouldn't rush Williams back, but they really need him back after the performance from the Packers QBs in Week 5.

Fortunately, this update from Rapoport points to the Bears' franchise quarterback being back in action for Week 6 against the Falcons.

Nothing is confirmed just yet, and he'll need to suit up during practice this week to prove he's good to go. But based on his pre-game workout and this report, Williams is clearly trending in the right direction.

The 3-2 Bears are tied for last place in the NFC North with the Packers and Detroit Lions , sitting 2.0 games back of the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings.

If the Bears want any chance of winning the division again, they're going to need to get Williams back as soon as possible. That looks possible, if not likely, as Williams returning to the field for Week 6 is very much in play.
